result.topic_en: Calculations dated December 1857 on an integral representation of a function $\varphi_m(y)$ with power factors $(y-a)(y-a')$, the change of variable $s=e^{\theta i/2}$ with a discriminant computation, the Poisson-kernel sum $\frac12+\sum\cos m\theta\,\sigma^m$, and a resulting double integral involving distances $S=(x-s)^2+y^2+z^2$, $T=(a-t)^2+b^2+c^2$, apparently a potential-theory problem.
result.transcription:
December 1857.
[-$\varphi(y)=\frac{i}{\pi}4^{m+\frac12}\frac{\Pi(m-\frac12)^2(-1)^{m+1}}{\Pi(2m-\frac12)\Pi(-\frac12)}((y-a)(y-a'))^{-m-\frac12}$-]
[-$\frac{i}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\frac{\cos 2m\theta\,\partial\theta}{\sqrt{(z-a)(z'-a')+(\frac{z-z'}{2i})^2\sin\theta^2}}$-]
$\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\frac{e^{m\theta i}\,\partial\theta}{\sqrt{(z-a)(z'-a')-(a-a')(z-z')\sin(\frac{\theta}{2})^2}}=\frac{2i}{\pi}\int\partial y\,(z-y)(z'-y)^{-m-\frac12}((y-a)(y-a'))^{-m-\frac12}(a-a')^{m}(z-z')^{-m}$
$=\frac{4i}{\pi}\int_z^{z'}$
$(z-y)(z'-y)(a-a')s^2-(y-a)(y-a')(z-z')=[-z-]\,2f=0$
$y^2((a-a')s^2-(z-z'))+y(-s^2(a-a')(z+z')+(a+a')(z-z'))+zz'(a-a')s^2-aa'(z-z')=0$
$4(a_1^2-a_0a_2)=(a-a')^2(z-z')^2+s^2(a-a')(z-z')[-2(a+a')(z+z')+4aa'+4zz']$
$=s^2(a-a')(z-z')[(s-\frac1s)^2(a-a')(z-z')+4(z-a)(z'-a')]$
$\frac{\partial y}{\frac{\partial f}{\partial s}}=-\frac{\partial s}{\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}}=\frac{\partial y}{\sqrt{(z-y)(z'-y)(y-a)(y-a')}}$ [-$(z-z')(a-a')$-] [-$=\partial s$-]
$=-\frac{\partial s}{a_0y+a_1}=-\frac{\partial s}{\sqrt{a_1^2-a_0a_2}}=-\frac{\partial\log s}{\sqrt{(s-\frac1s)^2(a-a')(z-z')+(z-a)(z'-a')}}$ \quad $s=e^{\frac{\theta}{2}i}$ \quad $e^{m\theta i}=s^{2m}$
$\partial\theta=-2i\,\partial\log s$
$\partial_y\varphi_m(y)=\frac{4i}{\pi}(a-a')^{m}\partial_y\frac{1}{?}\int_a^{a'}\frac{\partial x}{z-y}\,((x-a)(x-a'))^{-m+\frac12}$ \quad [figure: closed curve around $a'$, $x$]
$\Sigma\cos m\theta\int\partial y\,((z-y)(z'-y))^{m-\frac12}(z-z')^{-m}\varphi_m(y)=$
$\cos m\theta\,((z-y)(z'-y))^{2m-\frac12}((x-a)(x-a'))^{-2m-\frac12}(a-a')^{2m}(z-z')^{-2m}=\frac12(x-a)$
$\frac12+\Sigma\cos m\theta\,\sigma^m=\frac12\left(\frac{1}{1-e^{\theta i}\sigma}+\frac{e^{-\theta i}\sigma}{1-e^{-\theta i}\sigma}\right)=\frac12\frac{1-\sigma^2}{1-2\cos\theta\,\sigma+\sigma^2}$ \quad $\sigma=\frac{(z-y)(z'-y)(a-a')}{(x-a)(x-a')(z-z')}=$
$\frac{2}{\pi\pi}\int_z^{z'}\partial y\int_\alpha^{\alpha'}\partial\xi\,\frac{1}{\xi-\eta}\,\frac{1-\sigma^2}{1-2\cos\theta\,\sigma+\sigma^2}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{(z-y)(z'-y)(x-a)(x-a')}}$ \quad $\varrho e^{-\theta i}=\frac{(x-s)^2+y^2+z^2}{(a-t)^2+b^2+c^2}\cdot\frac{b+ci}{y+zi}$
$=\frac{2}{\pi\pi}\int\partial s\int\partial\tau\,\frac{\partial t}{\sigma-\tau}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ }}$ \quad $\varrho=\frac{((x^2+y^2+z^2)-2xs+s^2)\sqrt{b^2+c^2}}{((a^2+b^2+c^2)-2at+t^2)\sqrt{y^2+z^2}}$
$=\frac{2}{\pi\pi}\int\frac{\partial s}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2-2xs+s^2}}\int\frac{\partial t}{\sigma-\tau}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2-2at+t^2}}\,\frac{1-\varrho^2}{1-2\cos\theta\,\varrho+\varrho^2}$ \quad $\cos\theta\sqrt{b^2+c^2}\sqrt{y^2+z^2}=by+cz$
$\varrho=\frac{x^2+y^2+z^2-2xs+s^2}{a^2+b^2+c^2-2at+t^2}\frac{\sqrt{b^2+c^2}}{\sqrt{y^2+z^2}}$ \quad $\cos\theta\sqrt{b^2+c^2}\sqrt{y^2+z^2}=by+cz$
$=\frac{2}{\pi\pi}\int\frac{\partial s}{\sqrt S}\int\frac{\partial t}{\sigma-\tau}\frac{1}{\sqrt T}\,\frac{T^2(y^2+z^2)-S^2(b^2+c^2)}{T^2(y^2+z^2)-2(by+cz)ST+S^2(b^2+c^2)}$ \quad $S=(x-s)^2+y^2+z^2$
$T=(a-t)^2+b^2+c^2$
$\frac{(yT+bS)+(zT+cS)i}{yT-bS+(zT-cS)i}$

Differential relation between $dy$ and $ds$ from implicit equation
